task: Write a short friendly note to put in my neighbor's mailbox. Their party went until about 1am last Saturday and I could hear it clearly. I'd like them to keep it down after 10pm next time, and I want it to sound neighborly, not angry.
rewrite:
ambition:     A good neighborhood mediator wouldn't send a complaint. They'd send a warm note that names one specific, easy ask (quiet after 10pm) and says outright that the neighbor is welcome to have people over.
agency:       The raw material is your own facts: last Saturday, noise until about 1am, clearly audible from your place. Only you know your name and how to reach you, so those are the only blanks.
acceleration: Use the standard mediation sequence: warm opening, one plain observation with no blame, the specific request, then an open door ("knock or text me if it ever gets loud"). Keep it to about 80-110 words so it fits on a card.
accuracy:     Nothing outside the model can check tone. The closest proxy is reading it as the neighbor would on their doorstep and asking whether any line sounds like an accusation. The note should contain no judgment words such as "inconsiderate" or "disturbing", and no effects you didn't state, such as lost sleep.

deeper task:
Write a short, friendly note to put in my neighbor's mailbox. Their party ran until about 1am last Saturday and I could hear it clearly from my place. I'd like them to keep it down after 10pm next time, and it should sound neighborly, not angry. Open warmly, state the date and time as a plain fact without blame, and make the 10pm request specific and easy to say yes to. Say they're welcome to have people over, and invite them to knock or text me if it ever gets loud so we can sort it out in the moment. Don't invent details I haven't given you, like lost sleep or a prior complaint. Sign it with my name and leave a blank only for my name and contact info. Write the finished note at about 80-110 words, with nothing around it.

answers.plain:
Hi neighbor,

I hope you're doing well! I'm [Your Name] from [address/unit]. It looks like you had a fun get-together last Saturday. I hope everyone had a great time.

I wanted to mention that the sound carried over to our place and was pretty clear until about 1am, which made it tough to sleep. I'm sure you didn't realize it. Would you mind keeping the noise down after 10pm next time? I'd really appreciate it.

Feel free to give me a heads-up before your next party. I'm happy to be flexible for the occasional special night. Thanks so much for understanding!

Warmly,
[Your Name]
[Phone number, optional]
answers.nudge:
## The note

> Hi neighbor!
>
> I'm [Name] from [address/unit, e.g., the blue house next door]. I wanted to say hi and mention something small, in case you didn't realize it.
>
> It sounded like you had a great party last Saturday. The music and voices carried over to our place until about 1am, though, and I had a hard time sleeping. I'm sure you didn't mean to keep anyone up.
>
> If you have another get-together, would you mind turning the music down and moving things inside after 10pm? And if you give me a heads-up, I'm happy to plan around it, or I'll even come say hi. I'd rather talk about it than let it bug me.
>
> Thanks so much! You can reach me anytime at [phone/email].
>
> Warmly,
> [Name]

## Why it's written this way

- **It assumes good intent.** "In case you didn't realize" and "I'm sure you didn't mean to" give them a way to fix it without feeling accused.
- **It's specific.** Naming the day, the 1am end time, and the 10pm cutoff makes it a clear, reasonable request rather than a vague complaint.
- **It offers a two-way channel.** Your contact info and the offer to get a heads-up make it easy for them to reach you directly. That helps keep a small issue from turning into a feud or a call to the landlord or city.
- **It acknowledges the fun.** One friendly line about the party signals that you aren't against them having people over.

## Delivery tips

- **Handwrite it** if you can. A handwritten note feels more personal than a printed one.
- **Sign it with your name and address.** An anonymous note about noise reads as passive-aggressive.
- **Consider introducing yourself in person first** next time you see them. If you can, a brief friendly chat is better than any note.
- **Keep a private record** of the date and time of any future incidents, in case the issue repeats and you need to go to a landlord or HOA.

## Shorter version, if you prefer

> Hi! I'm [Name] next door. Sounded like a fun party Saturday. It carried over to our place until about 1am, though. Next time, could you wrap up the loud stuff by 10pm? A quick text beforehand is welcome, and I'm happy to chat anytime: [phone]. Thanks, neighbor!

I can adjust the tone to be more casual or more formal if you'd like. I can also tailor it if you live in an apartment, where a lease or quiet-hours rule gives you something to reference.
